title: The derived category of a symmetric abelian monoidal category is symmetric
statement: Let $C$ be an abelian symmetric monoidal category whose tensor product is additive in each variable. Write $K(C)$ for its homotopy category of cochain complexes, $D(C)$ for its derived category, and $Q_h:K(C)\to D(C)$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume the usual direct-sum total tensor of cochain complexes, with differential $d_A\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_B$ on degrees $(p,q)$, unsigned associator induced by reassociation and reindexing, and the usual unitors, exists and induces the total monoidal structure on $K(C)$; the iterated tensor coproducts have their usual universal properties, so triple-summand inclusions detect equality. Assume $Q_h$ carries the derived monoidal structure of [lem-asd-derived-category-braided]: its tensor bifunctor $T(X,Y)=X\otimes^L Y$, with comparison $\varepsilon_{A,B}:T(Q_hA,Q_hB)\to Q_h(A\otimes B)$, is the binary left derived functor of $F(A,B)=Q_h(A\otimes B)$. Here the binary universal property means that for every bifunctor $G:D(C)\times D(C)\to D(C)$ the map $\operatorname{Nat}(G,T)\to\operatorname{Nat}(G\circ(Q_h\times Q_h),F)$, $u\mapsto\varepsilon\circ(u\circ(Q_h\times Q_h))$, is bijective. As part of the derived monoidal structure, the two parenthesized triple tensors and the right-parenthesized fourfold tensor, with composite comparisons built from $\varepsilon$, have the corresponding three- and four-variable universal properties, and tensoring on either side with $Q_h\mathbf1$, with comparisons $\varepsilon_{\mathbf1,-}$ and $\varepsilon_{-,\mathbf1}$, has the corresponding one-variable universal properties. Here the corresponding $n$-variable property means that for every $n$-variable functor $G$, postcomposition with the specified comparison gives a bijection from natural transformations into the derived $n$-fold tensor to natural transformations from $G\circ Q_h^{\times n}$ into the localized ordinary $n$-fold tensor. The associator and unitors are those induced by these properties. Let $\beta$ be the braiding induced from the Koszul braiding by the binary universal property [lem-asd-derived-category-braided]. Then $\beta_{Y,X}\circ\beta_{X,Y}=\operatorname{id}_{X\otimes^L Y}$ for all $X,Y\in D(C)$; thus this specific derived braiding is symmetric.

proof.text: Apply [lem-asd-homotopy-category-koszul-braided] with $I=\mathbf Z$, $c(p,p\prime)\iff p\prime=p+1$, differential signs $(-1)^p$ and flip signs $(-1)^{pq}$. Its total tensor hypotheses hold by assumption; its differential and coherence sign equations follow from $(p+1)q=pq+q$, $p(q+1)=pq+p$, $p(q+r)=pq+pr$ and $(p+q)r=pr+qr$ modulo two. It gives the Koszul chain isomorphism and its descent to $K(C)$. Its involutivity follows from the stated summand formula. Write $b_{A,B}$ for the homotopy braiding and $c_{U,V}$ for the symmetry of $C$. On the summand $A^p\otimes B^q$, applying the chain braiding twice gives $(-1)^{pq+qp}(c_{B^q,A^p}\circ c_{A^p,B^q})=\operatorname{id}$. Indeed, $pq+qp=2pq$ is even, including for negative integers, and the parenthesized composite is identity by the assumed symmetry of $C$. In each total degree the coproduct injections determine any map out of that direct sum, so these equalities give equality of the chain maps. The quotient functor to $K(C)$ preserves identities and composition, and every homotopy object is represented by a complex. Consequently $b_{B,A}\circ b_{A,B}=\operatorname{id}_{A\otimes B}$ for all $A,B\in K(C)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-asd-derived-category-braided]: symmetry of $C$ supplies its braiding, and its graded tensor, binary, triple, quadruple and unit derivability hypotheses are exactly the assumed derived monoidal structure. Its induced braiding is obtained from $b$ by the binary left-derived universal property. Spell out its defining comparison equation, without requiring $\varepsilon$ to be invertible. Put $T^{\mathrm{op}}(X,Y)=T(Y,X)$. The natural transformation $T^{\mathrm{op}}(Q_hA,Q_hB)\to F(A,B)$ given by $Q_h(b_{B,A})\circ\varepsilon_{B,A}$ has a unique lift $\sigma:T^{\mathrm{op}}\to T$. The induced braiding has component $\beta_{Q_hA,Q_hB}=\sigma_{Q_hB,Q_hA}$, so its defining equation is $\varepsilon_{B,A}\circ\beta_{Q_hA,Q_hB}=Q_h(b_{A,B})\circ\varepsilon_{A,B}$. This is precisely the universal-property construction named by the cited node (upstream flipLift and its factorization). It uses the universal property with target $T$ only, and requires no separate derivability assumption on $T^{\mathrm{op}}$.

proof.text:
The double braiding $u_{X,Y}=\beta_{Y,X}\circ\beta_{X,Y}$ is a natural endomorphism of $T$, since $\beta$ is a natural braiding. For $A,B\in K(C)$ apply the preceding comparison equation twice, then use functoriality and the involutivity proved in step 1:
$$\varepsilon_{A,B}\circ u_{Q_hA,Q_hB}=Q_h(b_{B,A})\circ\varepsilon_{B,A}\circ\beta_{Q_hA,Q_hB}=Q_h(b_{B,A})\circ Q_h(b_{A,B})\circ\varepsilon_{A,B}=\varepsilon_{A,B}.$$
The identity natural endomorphism of $T$ has the same image under postcomposition with $\varepsilon$.

proof.text: Apply the binary universal property in the statement with $G=T$. Its injectivity identifies the natural endomorphisms $u$ and $\operatorname{id}_T$, because step 3 identifies their images as natural transformations on $K(C)\times K(C)$. Evaluating this equality at arbitrary derived objects $X,Y$ gives $\beta_{Y,X}\circ\beta_{X,Y}=\operatorname{id}_{T(X,Y)}$. This proves symmetry for the specified induced braiding, rather than only on chosen representatives. The argument does not cancel the comparison morphisms or assume tensoring arbitrary complexes preserves quasi-isomorphisms.
